title: Trace calculus for finite-potent linear endomorphisms
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $V$ a $k$-vector space, of arbitrary dimension. Finite-dimensionality is as in [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace], and ordinary trace as in [def-weil-endomorphism-trace]. Call $T\in\operatorname{End}_k(V)$ finite-potent if $T^N(V)$ is finite-dimensional for some $N\ge1$. There exists a canonical scalar $\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp},V}(T)$: whenever $U\subset V$ is finite-dimensional, $T(U)\subset U$ and $T^N(V)\subset U$, it equals $\operatorname{Tr}_k(T|_U)$, independently of $U,N$. It agrees with ordinary trace when $V$ is finite-dimensional and is zero for a nilpotent endomorphism. For every $T$-stable subspace $L\subset V$, the restriction $T|_L$ and the induced map $\overline T$ on $V/L$ are finite-potent and
$$\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp},V}(T)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp},L}(T|_L)+\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp},V/L}(\overline T).$$
For $c\in k$, $\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp}}(cT)=c\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp}}(T)$. If $a:V\to W$, $b:W\to V$ are $k$-linear and $ba$ is finite-potent, then $ab$ is finite-potent and $\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp},V}(ba)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp},W}(ab)$. Finally, if $T_1,\ldots,T_r$ are endomorphisms of $V$ such that every $T_iT_j$ has finite-dimensional image, then all $T_i$ and $\sum_i T_i$ are finite-potent and
$$\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp}}\left(\sum_iT_i\right)=\sum_i\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp}}(T_i).$$

source.place: §1, pp. 149–150, T1–T5; T4 specialized to pairwise products of finite rank

proof.text: Fix a finite-potent $T$ and choose $n\ge1$ with $U_0=T^n(V)$ finite-dimensional [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace]. The identity $T(T^nx)=T^n(Tx)$ shows that $U_0$ is $T$-stable. Define a candidate scalar $t=\operatorname{tr}(T|_{U_0})$ using [def-weil-endomorphism-trace]. No stabilization of the descending images is needed for this construction.

Let $U$ be any finite-dimensional $T$-stable subspace containing $T^N(V)$, where $N\ge1$. Set $m=\max(n,N)$ and $R=T^m(V)$. The identity $T^m=T^nT^{m-n}=T^NT^{m-N}$ puts $R$ in both $U_0$ and $U$; also $T(R)\subset R$. For each $X\in\{U_0,U\}$, the inclusion and quotient give the exact sequence $0\to R\to X\to X/R\to0$ of finite-dimensional spaces. The restriction of $T$ preserves this sequence, and the induced endomorphism $T_{X/R}$ satisfies $T_{X/R}^m(x+R)=T^mx+R=0$. Apply [lem-pc-finite-dimensional-trace-exact] and [lem-pc-finite-dimensional-nilpotent-trace] to obtain $\operatorname{tr}(T|_X)=\operatorname{tr}(T|_R)+0$. Thus the two choices have the same trace. In particular $t$ is independent of $n,U_0$ and equals the trace on every permitted $U$, and this property uniquely determines $t$. Write it $\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp},V}(T)$.

When $V$ is finite-dimensional, $U=V$ is a permitted subspace, giving ordinary trace. If $T^e=0$ for some $e\ge1$, then $U=0$ is permitted and its trace is the empty diagonal sum, namely zero, by [def-weil-endomorphism-trace]. These arguments also cover the zero vector space and the zero endomorphism.

Let $L\subset V$ be $T$-stable and let $q:V\to V/L$ be the quotient. Put $A=U_0\cap L$ and $B=q(U_0)$. These are finite-dimensional: $A$ is a subspace of $U_0$ and $B$ is spanned by the images of any finite spanning set of $U_0$. They are stable under $T|_L$ and $\overline T$ respectively. Indeed stability follows by applying $T$ or $qT=\overline Tq$. Moreover $(T|_L)^n(L)=T^n(L)\subset A$, and $\overline T^n(V/L)=q(T^nV)=B$. These inclusions prove finite potency of both induced operators. The sequence $0\to A\to U_0\xrightarrow{q}B\to0$ is exact: inclusion is injective, the last map is surjective by the definition of $B$, and its kernel is exactly $U_0\cap L$. Apply [lem-pc-finite-dimensional-trace-exact] to its compatible restrictions of $T$. The comparison established in step 2 identifies the three ordinary traces with their finite-potent traces, giving the asserted additivity.

For $c\in k$, the same subspace $U_0$ is stable under $cT$, and $(cT)^n(V)\subset U_0$ since $(cT)^nx=c^nT^nx$. Hence $cT$ is finite-potent. On a basis of $U_0$, the diagonal entries of $(cT)|_{U_0}$ are $c$ times those of $T|_{U_0}$. The definition [def-weil-endomorphism-trace] and step 2 give $\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp}}(cT)=c\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp}}(T)$. This works also for $c=0$.

Let $a:V\to W$ and $b:W\to V$ be linear with $ba$ finite-potent. Choose $n\ge1$ and $A=(ba)^n(V)$ finite-dimensional, and set $B=a(A)$. Then $ba(A)\subset A$, $a(A)\subset B$ and $b(B)=ba(A)\subset A$, so $ab(B)\subset B$. Also $(ab)^{n+1}=a(ba)^nb$ gives $(ab)^{n+1}(W)\subset B$, proving that $ab$ is finite-potent because the image $B$ of finite-dimensional $A$ is finite-dimensional. The restricted maps $a_0:A\to B$ and $b_0:B\to A$ satisfy $b_0a_0=(ba)|_A$ and $a_0b_0=(ab)|_B$ by evaluation on vectors. Apply [lem-pc-finite-dimensional-trace-cyclic], then step 2 on $A$ and $B$, to obtain the required equality of finite-potent traces.

For the finite family in the statement set $S=\sum_iT_i$ and $U=\sum_{i,j}\operatorname{im}(T_iT_j)$. A finite union of finite spanning sets for these images spans $U$, so $U$ is finite-dimensional. For each $\ell$, a generator $T_iT_jx$ of $U$ is sent by $T_\ell$ to $(T_\ell T_i)(T_jx)$, which lies in $\operatorname{im}(T_\ell T_i)\subset U$; linearity therefore gives $T_\ell(U)\subset U$ and $S(U)\subset U$. We have $T_i^2(V)\subset U$ and $S^2x=\sum_{i,j}T_iT_jx\in U$. Thus each $T_i$ and $S$ is finite-potent. By step 2 all their traces are computed on $U$. Restriction commutes with the finite sum, and summing diagonal entries on a single basis of $U$ gives $\operatorname{tr}(S|_U)=\sum_i\operatorname{tr}(T_i|_U)$ by [def-weil-endomorphism-trace]. This is the asserted sum formula. If $r=0$, then $U=0$ and both sides are zero.

lean.statement: theorem finitePotent_trace_calculus (k : Type u) [Field k] (V : Type v) [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] : (∀ (T : Module.End k V), T.IsFinitePotent → ∀ (U : Submodule k V), FiniteDimensional k U → ∀ (hU : ∀ x ∈ U, T x ∈ U) (N : ℕ), 1 ≤ N → LinearMap.range (T ^ N) ≤ U → T.tateTrace = LinearMap.trace k U (T.restrict hU)) ∧ (∀ (T : Module.End k V), T.IsFinitePotent → ∃! t : k, ∀ (U : Submodule k V), FiniteDimensional k U → ∀ (hU : ∀ x ∈ U, T x ∈ U) (N : ℕ), 1 ≤ N → LinearMap.range (T ^ N) ≤ U → t = LinearMap.trace k U (T.restrict hU)) ∧ (∀ [FiniteDimensional k V] (T : Module.End k V), T.tateTrace = LinearMap.trace k V T) ∧ (∀ (T : Module.End k V), IsNilpotent T → T.IsFinitePotent ∧ T.tateTrace = 0) ∧ (∀ (T : Module.End k V), T.IsFinitePotent → ∀ (L : Submodule k V) (hL : ∀ x ∈ L, T x ∈ L), IsFinitePotent (T.restrict hL) ∧ IsFinitePotent (L.mapQ L T hL) ∧ T.tateTrace = tateTrace (T.restrict hL) + tateTrace (L.mapQ L T hL)) ∧ (∀ (T : Module.End k V), T.IsFinitePotent → ∀ c : k, (c • T).IsFinitePotent ∧ (c • T).tateTrace = c * T.tateTrace) ∧ (∀ (W : Type w) [AddCommGroup W] [Module k W] (a : V →ₗ[k] W) (b : W →ₗ[k] V), IsFinitePotent (b ∘ₗ a) → IsFinitePotent (a ∘ₗ b) ∧ tateTrace (b ∘ₗ a) = tateTrace (a ∘ₗ b)) ∧ (∀ (r : ℕ) (T : Fin r → Module.End k V), (∀ i j : Fin r, FiniteDimensional k (LinearMap.range (T i * T j))) → (∀ i : Fin r, (T i).IsFinitePotent) ∧ (∑ i : Fin r, T i).IsFinitePotent ∧ (∑ i : Fin r, T i).tateTrace = ∑ i : Fin r, (T i).tateTrace)
